_comment: Single source of truth for mapping OpenClaw events to project buckets.
Used by code/openclaw_cost_tracker.py (resolve_project) and the web UI card.
(openclaw_usage.py is a deprecated shim; do not import as the entry point.)
Lookup order at event time:
1. If kind == 'cron'      → cron_jobs[cronJobId]
2. If kind in ('discord', 'telegram') and channel looks like a Discord id → discord_channels[channel]
3. If kind starts with 'dreaming-narrative-' → 'open-claw-dreaming'
4. kinds[kind] as a fallback (e.g. kind='openai' → 'media-generation', kind='main' → 'selena-direct')
5. default → 'uncategorized'
Subagent policy: subagent events are NEVER routed to a 'selena-subagent' project.
Instead they carry is_subagent=true and inherit the project of their parent kind
(usually the project the cron was running on). The web UI shows a '🔁 subagent'
badge next to subagent events so the work is visible without polluting the project list.
Schema v2 (2026-06-09, per Arcurus #cost-tracker):
- Projects may declare `parentProject: <slug>` to nest under a parent.
- The parent declares `is_parent: true` and `children: [<slug>, ...]`.
- rollup_display (optional) hints how the UI should render the rollup.
- First real use: open-world-selena is split into open-world-dev (OpenClaw-side) + open-world-running (LLM calls from the live sim).
When you add a new cron, channel, or kind bucket: edit this file, restart
selena-api.service, run `python3 code/openclaw_cost_tracker.py sync` to recompute the events.
Use `python3 code/openclaw_cost_tracker.py suggest-projects` to find unmapped items and
`python3 code/openclaw_cost_tracker.py mapping` to print the active mapping.
updated_by: selena (per Arcurus 2026-06-09 #cost-tracker: split open-world-selena into open-world-dev + open-world-running)

cron_jobs._comment_cron: Resolved by event.cronJobId. The resolver tries the full id first, then the 8-char prefix. Source: ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json + Arcurus 2026-06-07 #cost-tracker.

discord_channels._comment_channels: Resolved by event.channel (the actual Discord snowflake) for kind in (discord, telegram). Names verified against selena-project-2/orchestrator/overseer.py CHANNELS map + MEMORY.md (2026-06-07).
discord_channels._1494781163498246144_name: #selena-project-ops (slow + fast heartbeat deliver here per Arcurus 2026-06-07)

kinds._comment_kinds: Resolved by event.kind when no cron_job_id / channel match. Subkinds like 'dreaming-narrative-deep-6ac5bae53741' are handled separately by the prefix rule in resolve_project().

projects._comment_projects:
openlife is split into 2 projects:
    - openlife-moderation: the ALWAYS-SCHEDULED moderation cron (critical, runs on its own timer)
    - openlife-community: the openlife Discord channels for community work

selena-project.title: selena-project
selena-project.description: Selena's main coordination project: API server, web UI, cost tracker, todos, code, cron workers (selena-project-worker, heartbeats, announcer, daily-cost-report, voice-poem, memory-loose-ends).
selena-project.worker_cron_schedule_note: cron expr now "0 5 * * *" (was "0 * * * *"); trigger script fires it when conditions met. Daily run = housekeeping fallback.

open-world-selena.title: open-world-selena
open-world-selena.description: PARENT. The Rust open-world simulation as a whole: axum HTTP server, entity scheduler, world state. Per Arcurus 2026-06-09 #cost-tracker, this project is split into two children: 'open-world-dev' (OpenClaw-side workers + Discord activity) and 'open-world-running' (LLM calls made by the live simulation). The parent itself is no longer a direct attribution target — events land on one of the two children and roll up here for display.
open-world-selena.rollup_display: show children indented under the parent in the projects tab + per-project cost tables

open-world-dev.title: open-world-dev
open-world-dev.description: CHILD of open-world-selena. OpenClaw-side dev work for the world simulation: the selena-open-world-worker cron (job 13b68e52) that monitors the world, generates digests, posts to #openworld + #openworld-log. LLM calls made by that worker also land here. Does NOT include the LLM calls generated inside the running simulation (those go to open-world-running).
open-world-dev.worker_cron_schedule_note: cron expr now "0 13 * * *" (was "15 * * * *"); trigger script fires it when conditions met. Daily run = housekeeping fallback.

open-world-running.title: open-world-running
open-world-running.description: CHILD of open-world-selena. LLM calls made by the LIVE open-world simulation (the Rust binary in main.rs ~line 2208, in record_llm_call_async). Every entity action that triggers a model call is tagged with project=open-world-running so we can measure how much of the budget the world itself burns, separately from the dev worker. Override the project name with the OW_LLM_PROJECT env var on the open-world-selena service.

open-claw-dreaming.title: open-claw-dreaming
open-claw-dreaming.description: Memory Dreaming: nightly reflection cycle that consolidates short-term memory into long-term. Memory Dreaming Promotion cron + dreaming-narrative-* session kinds. Volume: 4 events in 30d sample (~0.4% of LLM calls); SOUL.md target is 15% of priority budget — underweight right now.
open-claw-dreaming.worker_cron_schedule_note: ALWAYS-SCHEDULED: cron expr 0 3 * * * (nightly). Checks 95% gate only. No trigger.

media-generation.title: media-generation
media-generation.description: Non-agent LLM work: image gen, music gen, TTS, transcription. Driven by mmx-cli + openai-whisper / openai image skills. Volume: 72 events in 30d sample (~7% of LLM calls).

selena-direct.title: selena-direct
selena-direct.description: Direct Arcurus ↔ Selena conversations: webchat, Telegram, direct Discord messages. Always subagent=false (Arcurus is the agent driver). Volume: low — 1 event in 30d sample; this bucket spikes only when Arcurus chats live, which is the human-driven session layer.

uncategorized.title: uncategorized
uncategorized.description: Catch-all for events that didn't resolve. 52 events in 30d sample (~5% of LLM calls) — needs review. Run `python3 code/openclaw_cost_tracker.py suggest-projects` to see which cron jobs / channels / kinds landed here and what new project bucket they'd fit into.

project-lunaris.title: lunar (Project Lunaris)
project-lunaris.description: project-lunaris: orchestrator, overseer, optimisation manager, lunar-budget-guardian, shady-hourly-monitor. The 'shibes' web UI + reflection loop. Canonical name is now project-lunaris.
project-lunaris.worker_cron_schedule_note: cron expr now "0 9 * * *" (was "30 * * * *"); trigger script fires it when conditions met. Daily run = housekeeping fallback.

selena-discord-direct.title: Selena (Discord direct)
selena-discord-direct.description: Direct Discord DMs with Selena (not in any server channel). Pseudo-channel route for kind=discord sessions without a server-channel id.

selena-telegram-direct.title: Selena (Telegram direct)
selena-telegram-direct.description: Direct Telegram DMs with Selena. Pseudo-channel route for kind=telegram sessions.

openlife-moderation.title: Openlife Moderation
openlife-moderation.description: Openlife Reborn Discord moderation cron (openlife-moderation-check). ALWAYS-SCHEDULED at 0 4 * * *. Critical: runs on its own timer, checks the 95% gate only. The trigger script does NOT fire this — it has its own systemd timer.
openlife-moderation.worker_cron_schedule_note: ALWAYS-SCHEDULED (critical): cron expr 0 4 * * *. Checks 95% gate only. Not in trigger script.

openlife-community.title: Openlife Community
openlife-community.description: OpenLife Reborn Discord community channels (#openlife, #openlife-log, #moderation). Community discussions and reports — distinct from the moderation cron which has its own project.
